sections.title: Section I
sections.instructions: Attempt Questions 1 to 10. Allow about 15 minutes for this section.

stem.t: Using the substitution $t = \tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, the equation $4\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta = 3$ can be written as which quadratic equation in $t$?

sampleAnswer.t: With $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1 - t^2}{1 + t^2}$ and $\sin\theta = \dfrac{2t}{1 + t^2}$: $4(1 - t^2) + 3(2t) = 3(1 + t^2)$, which rearranges to $7 t^{2} - 6 t - 1 = 0$.

classification.content: The t-formulae

stem.t: Two particles are projected at the same instant from the same point, with the same speed, at angles of $50^\circ$ and $75^\circ$ to the horizontal. While both are in flight, the line joining them makes a constant acute angle with the horizontal.

sampleAnswer.t: The positions differ by $Vt(\cos\beta - \cos\alpha)\underset{\sim}{i} + Vt(\sin\beta - \sin\alpha)\underset{\sim}{j}$ (the $\tfrac12gt^2$ terms cancel). This is a multiple of $-\sin\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\,\underset{\sim}{i} + \cos\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\,\underset{\sim}{j}$, which is perpendicular to the direction at angle $\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2} = 62.5^\circ$. So the line makes an angle of $90^\circ - 62.5^\circ = 27.5^\circ$ with the horizontal.

classification.content: Projectile motion in vector form; relative position

stem.t: The graph of $y = f(x)$ is shown.

sampleAnswer.t: For $x \ge 0$ the graph of $y = f(|x|)$ is the same as that of $y = f(x)$, and the part for $x < 0$ is its reflection in the $y$-axis. Only graph B has this form.

classification.content: Graphs of y = f(|x|) and related functions

stem.t: What is the range of the function $y = 4\cos^{-1}(5x) - 5$?

sampleAnswer.t: $\cos^{-1}$ takes every value from $0$ to $\pi$ on its domain, so $4\cos^{-1}(5x)$ takes every value from $0$ to $4\pi$. Subtract 5.

classification.content: Inverse trigonometric functions; range

stem.t: What is the value of $\dfrac{d}{dx}\,\tan^{-1}{\left(\dfrac{3 x}{4} \right)}$ at $x = \dfrac{8}{3}$?

sampleAnswer.t: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\,\tan^{-1}{\left(\dfrac{3 x}{4} \right)} = \dfrac{12}{9 x^{2} + 16}$, which equals $\dfrac{3}{20}$ at $x = \dfrac{8}{3}$.

classification.content: Derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions

stem.t: When the polynomial $P(x)$ is divided by $x + 3$ the remainder is $0$, and when it is divided by $x - 2$ the remainder is $-1$.
What is the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $(x + 3)(x - 2)$?

sampleAnswer.t: The remainder has the form $mx + c$, and $P(x) = (x + 3)(x - 2)Q(x) + mx + c$. Then $P(-3) = 0$ and $P(2) = -1$ give $-3m + c = 0$ and $2m + c = -1$, so $m = - \dfrac{1}{5}$ and $c = - \dfrac{3}{5}$.

classification.content: Remainder theorem; division by a quadratic

stem.t: Which differential equation could have the slope field shown?

sampleAnswer.t: At $(2, 2)$ the slope in the field is about $-4$, which matches $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -xy$ (the other equations give $4, 5, \dfrac{2}{5}$ there).

classification.content: Slope fields

stem.t: A statement $S(n)$ about positive integers $n$ is such that $S(2)$ is true, and whenever $S(k)$ is true, $S(k + 3)$ is also true.
For which positive integers $n$ must $S(n)$ be true?

blocks.t: exactly those $n$ that leave remainder 2 on division by 3

sampleAnswer.t: Starting from $S(2)$ and adding 3 any number of times reaches exactly the integers with the same remainders on division by 3 as the starting values, that is, remainder 2. Nothing in the information forces $S(n)$ for any other $n$.

classification.content: Mathematical induction; what a step proves

stem.t: The tangent to the curve $y = 7x^{8}$ at the point where $x = 2$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$.

sampleAnswer.t: At $x = 2$ the gradient is $7 \times 8 \times 2^{7}$ and $y = 7 \times 2^{8}$. The tangent meets $y = 0$ where $x = 2 - \dfrac{y}{y'} = 2 - \dfrac{2}{8} = \dfrac{7}{4}$.

classification.content: Tangents; derivatives of powers and exponentials

stem.t: Which expression is equal to $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{n}k\dbinom{n}{k}3^{k}$ for every positive integer $n$?

sampleAnswer.t: Differentiate $(1 + x)^n = \sum_k \dbinom{n}{k}x^k$: $n(1 + x)^{n-1} = \sum_k k\dbinom{n}{k}x^{k-1}$. Multiply by $x$ and put $x = 3$.

classification.content: Binomial theorem; sums of binomial coefficients

sections.title: Section II
sections.instructions: Attempt Questions 11 to 14. Allow about 1 hour and 45 minutes for this section. Show relevant mathematical reasoning and/or calculations.

parts.label: (a)

prompt.t: Find all values of $k$ for which the polynomial $x^{3} + 6x^{2} + k$ has three different real zeros.

text.t: Provides the correct values with justification
Finds both turning values in terms of $k$

sampleAnswer.t: Let $P(x) = x^{3} + 6x^{2} + k$. Then $P'(x) = 3x^2 + 12 x = 3(x + 4)x$, so $P$ has a local maximum at $x = -4$ and a local minimum at $x = 0$, with $P(-4) = k + 32$ and $P(0) = k$. A cubic with positive leading coefficient has three different real zeros exactly when its local maximum value is positive and its local minimum value is negative: $P(-4) > 0$ and $P(0) < 0$. Hence $-32 < k < 0$.

classification.content: Polynomials; number of real zeros using turning points

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: exact distinct-real-root count of x^3+6x^2+k on a rational grid k in [-60,30] and at k=-32,0 and 1e-6 either side: three roots iff -32<k<0

prompt.t: Let $f(x) = \ln{\left(x^{2} + 4 \right)}$. The function $f$ is now restricted to the domain $x \ge 0$, where it has an inverse function $f^{-1}$. Find the domain of $f^{-1}$ and the gradient of the graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$ at the point where $x = \ln{\left(8 \right)}$.

text.t: Provides the correct domain and gradient
Finds the domain of the inverse

sampleAnswer.t: On $x \ge 0$, $f$ is increasing, with range $y \ge \ln{\left(4 \right)}$, which is the domain of $f^{-1}$. $f(2) = \ln{\left(8 \right)}$, so the point $\left(\ln{\left(8 \right)}, 2\right)$ is on $y = f^{-1}(x)$, and its gradient there is $\dfrac{1}{f'(2)} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 2$.

classification.content: Functions and calculus: inverse

prompt.t: Let $f(x) = (x + 4)^2 - 4$ for $x \ge -4$, and let $f^{-1}$ be its inverse function.
Find the coordinates of the points where the graphs of $y = f(x)$ and $y = f^{-1}(x)$ meet.

text.t: Explains why the graphs meet only on $y = x$, or solves $f(x) = x$ correctly

sampleAnswer.t: $f$ is increasing for $x \ge -4$. If $f(a) = b$ and $f^{-1}(a) = b$ then $f(b) = a$; if $a < b$ then $f(a) < f(b)$, that is, $b < a$, which is impossible, and similarly $a > b$ is impossible. So the graphs meet only on the line $y = x$, where $f(x) = x$: $x^2 + 7 x + 12 = 0$, so $(x + 4)(x + 3) = 0$. Both values satisfy $x \ge -4$, so the points are $(-4, -4)$ and $(-3, -3)$.

classification.content: Inverse functions; intersections with the inverse

parts.label: (d)

prompt.t: A ball is projected from a point $O$ on horizontal ground with speed $30$ m s$^{-1}$ at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. It passes through the point that is 30 m horizontally from $O$ and $35$ m above the ground. Take $g = 10$ m s$^{-2}$, and assume the ball's position at time $t$ is $Vt\cos\theta\,\underset{\sim}{i} + \left(Vt\sin\theta - 5t^2\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Find the two possible values of $\tan\theta$.

text.t: Solves the quadratic with a minor error
Obtains a correct quadratic equation in $\tan\theta$
Finds the time to reach the point

sampleAnswer.t: At horizontal distance $30$, $t = \dfrac{30}{30\cos\theta}$, so the height is $30\tan\theta - 5\sec^2\theta = 30\tan\theta - 5\left(1 + \tan^2\theta\right)$. Setting this equal to $35$ with $T = \tan\theta$: $\ 5T^2 - 30T + 40 = 0$. Its solutions are $T = 2$ and $T = 4$.

classification.content: Projectile motion; angles of projection through a given point

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: sign-change scan over theta of (height at 30 m)-35 using the stated position vector, bisected: tan = 2, 4

parts.label: (e)

prompt.t: Find the greatest value of $2\sin^2 x + 12\sin x\cos x - 2\cos^2 x$.

text.t: Writes the expression in the form $A + R\cos(2x - \alpha)$, or equivalent merit
Uses double-angle results to rewrite the expression

sampleAnswer.t: Using $\sin^2 x = \tfrac12(1 - \cos 2x)$, $\cos^2 x = \tfrac12(1 + \cos 2x)$ and $\sin x\cos x = \tfrac12\sin 2x$, the expression is $-2\cos 2x + 6\sin 2x$. Now $-2\cos 2x + 6\sin 2x = 2 \sqrt{10}\cos(2x - \alpha)$ for a suitable angle $\alpha$, and $\cos(2x - \alpha)$ takes every value from $-1$ to $1$. So the greatest value is $2 \sqrt{10}$.

classification.content: Double-angle results; auxiliary angle; extreme values

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: grid + golden-section maximum of the original expression over [0,2pi]: 6.324555320

parts.label: (a)

prompt.t: Find $y$ as a function of $x$, given that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x - y}$ and $y(0) = 1$.

sampleAnswer.t: $\displaystyle\int e^y\,dy = \int e^x\,dx$ gives $e^y = e^x + C$. At $x = 0$: $e^{1} = 1 + C$. Hence $y = \ln\left(e^x + e^{1} - 1\right)$.

classification.content: Separable differential equations

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: RK4 of dy/dx=e^(x-y), y(0)=1 vs the key at 8 points in [-3,3]

prompt.t: Use the substitution $t = \tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}$ to solve $\cos\theta + 13\sin\theta = 7$ for $0 \le \theta \le 2\pi$. Give your answers in exact form.

sampleAnswer.t: With $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1 - t^2}{1 + t^2}$ and $\sin\theta = \dfrac{2t}{1 + t^2}$ the equation becomes $8 t^{2} - 26 t + 6 = 0$, that is, $2 \left(t - 3\right) \left(4 t - 1\right) = 0$, so $t = \dfrac{1}{4}$ or $t = 3$. Checking $\theta = \pi$ (where $t$ is undefined): $\cos\pi = -1 \ne 7$, so it is not a solution. Since $0 \le \dfrac{\theta}{2} \le \pi$, the solutions are $\theta = 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$ and $\theta = 2\tan^{-1} 3$.

classification.content: The t-formulae; solving trigonometric equations

prompt.t: $OABC$ is a parallelogram with $\overrightarrow{OA} = \underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC} = \underset{\sim}{c}$. The point $P$ lies on $AB$ with $AP : PB = 2 : 5$, and $OP$ meets the diagonal $AC$ at $X$.

parts.label: (i)

prompt.t: Express $\overrightarrow{OP}$ in terms of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{c}$.

sampleAnswer.t: $\overrightarrow{AB} = \overrightarrow{OC} = \underset{\sim}{c}$, so $\overrightarrow{OP} = \underset{\sim}{a} + \dfrac{2}{7}\underset{\sim}{c}$.

classification.content: Vectors; ratios in a parallelogram

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: 6 random parallelograms: P on AB with AP:PB=2:5 located by division, equals a+2c/7 to 1e-12 componentwise

prompt.t: Find the ratio $OX : XP$.

text.t: Equates two expressions for $\overrightarrow{OX}$ and compares coefficients

sampleAnswer.t: $\overrightarrow{OX} = s\left(\underset{\sim}{a} + \dfrac{2}{7}\underset{\sim}{c}\right)$ for some $s$, and also $\overrightarrow{OX} = \underset{\sim}{a} + \mu(\underset{\sim}{c} - \underset{\sim}{a})$. Since $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{c}$ are not parallel, $s = 1 - \mu$ and $\dfrac{2}{7}s = \mu$, so $s = \dfrac{7}{9}$. Hence $OX : XP = \dfrac{7}{9} : \dfrac{2}{9} = 7 : 2$.

classification.content: Vectors; ratios in a parallelogram

prompt.t: The point $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$, and $AM$ meets $OB$ at $Y$. Find the ratio $OY : YB$.

text.t: Equates two expressions for $\overrightarrow{OY}$ and compares coefficients

sampleAnswer.t: $\overrightarrow{OM} = \underset{\sim}{c} + \tfrac12\underset{\sim}{a}$. A point of $AM$ is $\underset{\sim}{a} + v\left(\underset{\sim}{c} - \tfrac12\underset{\sim}{a}\right)$ and a point of $OB$ is $w(\underset{\sim}{a} + \underset{\sim}{c})$. Comparing coefficients, $v = w$ and $1 - \tfrac12v = w$, so $w = \tfrac23$. Hence $OY : YB = 2 : 1$.

classification.content: Vectors; ratios in a parallelogram

prompt.t: $n$ circles are drawn in the plane so that every two circles meet at exactly two points and no three circles pass through the same point. Let $R_n$ be the number of regions into which the circles divide the plane, so $R_1 = 2$. The diagram shows three such circles.
Explain why $R_{k+1} = R_k + 2k$ for $k \ge 1$.

text.t: Counts the intersection points on the new circle

sampleAnswer.t: The new circle meets each of the $k$ earlier circles at exactly two points, all different, so it has $2k$ points on it, which cut it into $2k$ arcs. Each arc splits one existing region into two, so $2k$ new regions are made and $R_{k+1} = R_k + 2k$.

classification.content: Recurrence relations; summing an arithmetic series; counting regions

prompt.t: Use part (i) to show that $R_n = n^2 - n + 2$ for all integers $n \ge 1$.

text.t: Adds the relations for $k = 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1$ and sums $2k$, or equivalent merit
Writes the relation $R_{k+1} - R_k = 2k$ for several consecutive values of $k$

sampleAnswer.t: By part (i), $R_{k+1} - R_k = 2k$ for $k = 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1$. Adding these $n - 1$ equations, all the terms $R_2, \ldots, R_{n-1}$ cancel and
using the sum of an arithmetic series. Since $R_1 = 2$, $R_n = n^2 - n + 2$. (For $n = 1$ the sum is empty and the formula gives $R_1 = 2$.)

classification.content: Recurrence relations; summing an arithmetic series; counting regions

parts.label: (iii)

prompt.t: Find the least number of circles needed to divide the plane into more than $1000$ regions.

sampleAnswer.t: We need $n^2 - n + 2 > 1000$. $R_{32} = 994$ and $R_{33} = 1058$, and $R_n$ increases with $n$, so the least number is $33$.

classification.content: Recurrence relations; summing an arithmetic series; counting regions

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: Euler-formula region count from real intersection geometry for n=1..8 random circles (matches n^2-n+2), then least n with count>1000

prompt.t: For $k \ge 1$ let $T_k = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{9 + k(k - 1)}\right)$, and let $S_n = T_1 + T_2 + \cdots + T_n$.
Show that $T_k = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{k}{3} - \tan^{-1}\dfrac{(k - 1)}{3}$.

sampleAnswer.t: Let $\alpha = \tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{3}k)$ and $\beta = \tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{3}(k - 1))$, so $0 \le \beta < \alpha < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Then $\tan(\alpha - \beta) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}k - \dfrac{1}{3}(k - 1)}{1 + \dfrac{1}{9}k(k - 1)} = \dfrac{3}{9 + k(k - 1)}$ (multiplying the numerator and denominator by $9$), and $0 < \alpha - \beta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $\alpha - \beta = T_k$.

classification.content: Inverse tangent; compound angles; telescoping sums

parts.label: (ii)

prompt.t: Find $S_n$ in terms of $n$.

text.t: Writes the sum using part (i) and notes the cancellation

sampleAnswer.t: By part (i) the sum telescopes: $S_n = \tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{3}n) - \tan^{-1}0 = \tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{3}n)$.

classification.content: Inverse tangent; compound angles; telescoping sums

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: direct summation of T_k at 30 digits for n=1..40

parts.label: (iii)

prompt.t: Find the limit of $S_n$ as $n \to \infty$.

sampleAnswer.t: As $n \to \infty$, $\dfrac{1}{3}n \to \infty$, so $S_n \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

classification.content: Inverse tangent; compound angles; telescoping sums

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: mpmath nsum of the series to 30 digits

parts.label: (iv)

prompt.t: Find the smallest $n$ for which $S_n > \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{20}$.

text.t: Writes the condition in terms of $\tan$ or $\cot$

sampleAnswer.t: $\tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{3}n) > \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{20}$ exactly when $\dfrac{1}{3}n > \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{20}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\tan \dfrac{1}{20}} \approx 19.983$, since $\tan$ is increasing on $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. So $n > 59.950$, and the smallest $n$ is $60$.

classification.content: Inverse tangent; compound angles; telescoping sums

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: direct partial sums at 40 digits: first n with S_n>pi/2-1/20

parts.label: (a)

prompt.t: Find the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(3 x^{3} + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{12}$.

sampleAnswer.t: The general term is $\dbinom{12}{k}\left(3 x^{3}\right)^{12 - k}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{k}$, in which the power of $x$ is $3(12 - k) - k$. This is zero when $k = 9$, so the term is $\dbinom{12}{9} \times 3^{3} = 5940$.

classification.content: Binomial expansion; term independent of x

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: SymPy expansion of (3x^3+1/x)^12, coefficient of x^0

parts.label: (b)

prompt.t: The random variable $X$ has a binomial distribution with mean $\dfrac{18}{5}$. It is given that $P(X = 3) = P(X = 4)$.
Find the number of trials $n$.

sampleAnswer.t: Equating $\dbinom{n}{3}p^{3}(1 - p)^{n - 3}$ and $\dbinom{n}{4}p^{4}(1 - p)^{n - 4}$ gives $(n - 3)p = 4(1 - p)$, so $p = \dfrac{4}{n + 1}$. Then $np = \dfrac{4n}{n + 1} = \dfrac{18}{5}$, which gives $n = 9$.

classification.content: Binomial probabilities and mean

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: exact Fractions: p=18/(5n); P(X=3)=P(X=4) only for n=9 over n=4..300

prompt.t: Let $f(x) = \dfrac{8}{x^{2} + 9}$. The diagram shows the graph of $y = f(x)$.
Find the coordinates of the stationary point of $y = f(x)$ and determine its nature.

text.t: Provides the correct points and their nature

sampleAnswer.t: $f'(x) = - \dfrac{16 x}{\left(x^{2} + 9\right)^{2}} = 0$ when $x = 0$. Using $f''(x) = \dfrac{48 \left(x^{2} - 3\right)}{\left(x^{2} + 9\right)^{3}}$: $f''\left(0\right) < 0$, so there is a local maximum at $\left(0, \dfrac{8}{9}\right)$.

classification.content: Functions and calculus: stationary, inflection, inverse

parts.label: (ii)

prompt.t: Find the $x$-coordinates of the points of inflection.

text.t: Provides the correct values with justification

sampleAnswer.t: $f''(x) = \dfrac{48 \left(x^{2} - 3\right)}{\left(x^{2} + 9\right)^{3}}$, which is zero and changes sign at $x = - \sqrt{3}, \sqrt{3}$.

classification.content: Functions and calculus: stationary, inflection, inverse

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p12.py: sign changes of f'' (SymPy exact) for f=8/(x^2+9)

prompt.t: The function $f$ is now restricted to the domain $x \ge 0$, where it has an inverse function $f^{-1}$. Find the domain of $f^{-1}$ and the gradient of the graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$ at the point where $x = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

text.t: Provides the correct domain and gradient
Finds the domain of the inverse

sampleAnswer.t: On $x \ge 0$, $f$ is decreasing, with range $0 < y \le \dfrac{8}{9}$, which is the domain of $f^{-1}$. $f(1) = \dfrac{4}{5}$, so the point $\left(\dfrac{4}{5}, 1\right)$ is on $y = f^{-1}(x)$, and its gradient there is $\dfrac{1}{f'(1)} = \dfrac{1}{- \dfrac{4}{25}} = - \dfrac{25}{4}$.

classification.content: Functions and calculus: stationary, inflection, inverse
